title: Organic Chemistry

notes.heading: 1. IUPAC Priority, Hybridization & Isomerism
notes.proseLatex: Principal functional-group priority runs $-\text{COOH} > -\text{SO}_3\text{H} > -\text{COOR} > -\text{COCl} > -\text{CONH}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{CHO} > >\text{C=O} > -\text{OH} > -\text{NH}_2 > \text{alkene/alkyne}$. Carbon hybridization sets $\sigma/\pi$ count and electronegativity: $sp\;(50\%\;s,\;\text{terminal alkyne acidic!}) > sp^2\;(33\%\;s) > sp^3\;(25\%\;s)$. Degree of unsaturation $\text{DBE} = C + 1 - \frac{H + X - N}{2}$ counts rings + $\pi$-bonds. Geometrical (*cis/trans*, $E/Z$) isomerism needs restricted rotation with $a\neq b$ on each end; optical activity requires absence of plane/centre of symmetry (chiral carbon $C^*$ gives up to $2^n$ stereoisomers, fewer when meso forms exist).

keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Count rings + pi bonds from molecular formulas and apply IUPAC suffix priority.

examples.problemLatex: Give the IUPAC name and $\sigma,\pi$ bond count of $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$.
stepsLatex: When double and triple bonds get identical locants $(1,4)$ from either end, ALKENE wins lowest locant: pent-1-en-4-yne.

notes.heading: 2. Electronic Effects, Carbocation Stability, Markovnikov & Ozonolysis
notes.proseLatex: Inductive ($\pm I$), resonance/mesomeric ($\pm M$), and hyperconjugation ($\alpha$-$\text{C--H}$ count!) stabilize carbocations and alkenes as $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^+$ (plus allylic/benzylic resonance), while carbanion stability reverses ($1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$). Unsymmetrical alkenes add $\text{HX}$ by Markovnikov's rule (rich get richer in $\text{H}$), whereas ONLY $\text{HBr}$ + organic peroxide ($\text{ROOR}$) flips to anti-Markovnikov radical addition (Kharasch effect; fails for $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$!). Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$, then $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) cleaves every $\text{C=C}$ cleanly into two $\text{C=O}$ carbonyls.

keyFormulas.label: Markovnikov vs Peroxide Kharasch & Hückel Aromaticity
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Predict alkene regioselectivity, ozonolysis products, and aromaticity.

notes.heading: 3. Diagnostic Tests (Lucas, Tollens, Iodoform) & Everyday Polymers
notes.proseLatex: Distinguishing tests: Lucas reagent ($\text{conc. HCl} + \text{anhyd. ZnCl}_2$) gives instant turbidity with $3^\circ$ alcohols, $\sim 5\text{ min}$ with $2^\circ$, and none at RT with $1^\circ$; Tollens' ammoniacal $\text{AgNO}_3$ silver mirror and Fehling's red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ test aldehydes (Fehling fails for benzaldehyde!); yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ iodoform ($\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$) identifies $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ (ethanol is the ONLY $1^\circ$ alcohol giving positive iodoform!). Aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-$\text{H}$ ($\text{HCHO}, \text{PhCHO}$) undergo Cannizzaro disproportionation, while those WITH $\alpha$-$\text{H}$ undergo Aldol condensation. Key polymers: Nylon-6,6 (hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid), Bakelite (phenol + $\text{HCHO}$), Teflon ($\text{CF}_2=\text{CF}_2$), natural rubber (*cis*-1,4-polyisoprene).

wbjeebTraps: Kharasch peroxide anti-Markovnikov effect works ONLY with $\text{HBr}$ — $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$ STILL obey Markovnikov even in presence of peroxides!
Ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) gives POSITIVE iodoform test, whereas methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) is NEGATIVE!

Acidity comparison: phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) $>$ water ($15.7$) $>$ alcohols ($16\text{--}18$) $>$ terminal alkynes ($25$); picric acid ($2,4,6$-trinitrophenol) even liberates $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{NaHCO}_3$ despite having no $-\text{COOH}$ group!

conceptPrimer.heading: IUPAC Priority & Parent Selection
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Principal-group priority: $-\text{COOH} > -\text{SO}_3\text{H} > -\text{COOR} > -\text{COCl} > -\text{CONH}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{CHO} > >\text{C=O} > -\text{OH} > -\text{NH}_2 >$ alkene/alkyne. The highest-priority group fixes the suffix and numbering direction. Micro-check: a molecule with $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{CHO}$ is an $\text{al}$, not an $\text{ol}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: $s$-Character, Hybridization & Acidity
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $sp$ ($50\%\,s$) $> sp^2$ ($33\%$) $> sp^3$ ($25\%$) in electronegativity: terminal alkyne $\text{C-H}$ ($sp$) is acidic enough for $\text{NaNH}_2$, alcohols are not. Acidity ladder: phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) $>$ water ($15.7$) $>$ alcohols ($16\text{--}18$) $>$ terminal alkynes ($25$); picric acid even liberates $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{NaHCO}_3$ with no $-\text{COOH}$ group. Micro-check: more $s$-character, closer electrons, more acidic.

conceptPrimer.heading: DBE: Counting Rings and $\pi$-Bonds
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\text{DBE} = C + 1 - \frac{H + X - N}{2}$: every ring or $\pi$-bond contributes one. Benzene: $6 + 1 - \frac{6}{2} = 4$ (ring + three doubles). Micro-check: halogens add to $H$; nitrogen subtracts from it; oxygen is invisible.

conceptPrimer.heading: Electronic Effects & Carbocation Stability
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Inductive ($\pm I$), resonance ($\pm M$) and hyperconjugation (count $\alpha$-C-H bonds!) stabilize carbocations and alkenes as $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^+$, boosted further by allylic/benzylic resonance; carbanions reverse ($1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$). Micro-check: benzylic beats $3^\circ$ when resonance is available.

conceptPrimer.heading: Markovnikov, Kharasch & Ozonolysis
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Unsymmetrical alkenes add HX with H going to the carbon already H-richer (Markovnikov). ONLY $\text{HBr}$ with peroxides ($\text{ROOR}$) flips to anti-Markovnikov radical addition (Kharasch) — $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$ never flip. Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3$, then $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) cleaves each $\text{C=C}$ into two carbonyls. Micro-check: peroxide + $\text{HI}$ still gives Markovnikov.

conceptPrimer.heading: Diagnostics, Disproportionation & Everyday Polymers
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Lucas ($\text{conc. HCl} + \text{anhyd.}\ \text{ZnCl}_2$): instant turbidity $3^\circ$, minutes $2^\circ$, none $1^\circ$ at RT. Tollens' silver mirror and Fehling's red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ catch aldehydes (Fehling fails for benzaldehyde). Iodoform ($\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$) flags $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$; ethanol is the ONLY $1^\circ$ alcohol positive. Aldehydes WITHOUT $\alpha$-H do Cannizzaro; WITH $\alpha$-H do Aldol. Polymers: Nylon-6,6 (diamine + adipic acid), Bakelite (phenol + $\text{HCHO}$), Teflon ($\text{CF}_2 = \text{CF}_2$), rubber (cis-1,4-polyisoprene). Micro-check: ethanol: Lucas-slow but iodoform-positive.

keyDefinitions.definition: Ring count plus $\pi$-bond count from the molecular formula.
Peroxide-driven radical addition of HBr giving anti-Markovnikov products.
Self-addition of aldehydes/ketones WITH $\alpha$-hydrogen under base.
Carbon bearing four different groups; source of optical activity.
Charge-separated contributor; stabilizes phenoxide and nitro groups.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: A molecule contains both $-\text{CHO}$ and $-\text{OH}$. Its principal suffix comes from:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $-\text{CHO}$ outranks $-\text{OH}$ in the IUPAC priority list.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Terminal alkyne C-H is more acidic than alkane C-H because:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Higher $s$-character holds electrons closer, stabilizing the conjugate base.
Treat Cl as H: $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$: $4 + 1 - 4 = 1$ (one $\pi$ or ring).
Benzylic resonance beats even $3^\circ$ inductive stabilization.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Which addition obeys the peroxide (Kharasch) anti-Markovnikov route?
mcqSelfTest.explanation: Only HBr: the radical chain is energetically viable for HBr alone.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene gives:
Lucas reagent gives INSTANT turbidity with:
mcqSelfTest.explanation: $3^\circ$ carbocation forms fastest; $2^\circ$ takes minutes, $1^\circ$ none at RT.

mcqSelfTest.stemLatex: Which $1^\circ$ alcohol gives a POSITIVE iodoform test?

mcqSelfTest.explanation: No $\alpha$-H, so base disproportionates it to benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

memoryHooks: Priority: COOH rules; OH barely beats NH$_2$.
Cations love alkyl; anions hate it.
Ozonolysis: double bond becomes two C=O.
Lucas: tertiary turbid in a blink.
commonMistakes: Forgetting halogens add to H and nitrogen subtracts in DBE.
Extending the peroxide effect to HCl or HI.
Claiming phenol is less acidic than an alcohol.
Expecting Fehling's solution to catch benzaldehyde.
Reversing carbocation and carbanion stability orders.
examChecklist: Check $\alpha$-H presence before Aldol or Cannizzaro.
Compute DBE with the $H + X - N$ correction.
Order carbocations, carbanions, and acidity ladders.
State Markovnikov vs Kharasch conditions exactly.
Assign Lucas, Tollens, Fehling, iodoform outcomes.
Choose Cannizzaro vs Aldol by $\alpha$-H presence.
Match polymers to monomers (Nylon-6,6, Bakelite, Teflon).
